lead.headline: People arrested 2+ years after arriving had ICE bond posted 7% of the time in Louisiana, 29% in Pennsylvania
lead.number: 7% in Louisiana, 12% in Texas, 29% in Pennsylvania, 2023-25, for people arrested 2+ years after entry.
lead.watch_out: The bond field fills when bond is posted, not when a judge sets it, and border states hold recent arrivals who can't get bond at all.

Typically, immigration judges would order such people released via an order of supervision, which stipulates conditions including regular check-ins with ICE. Then in June, the Supreme Court made a ruling that allowed ICE to send such people to a “third country.” A month later, DHS instituted a policy of mandatory detention, declaring that any immigrant who’d entered the U.S. “illegally” was ineligible for bond — even people who’ve been living in the country for decades. Around the same time, as immigrants who had been free for years went to routine ICE check-ins, ICE began arresting them, bringing them in “illegally, for the most part,” said Nora Ahmed, legal director of ACLU Louisiana.
